newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up in slow trading on Monday due to expectations of further rises on good market sentiment, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,418 yuan ($412) per tonne, rising two yuan. It opened at 3,416 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,412 and a high of 3,420 yuan.
May rose nine to 3,360, September 10 to 3,435, November 10 3,450 and January 1998 20 to 3,450 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 13,000 tonnes from 21,500 tonnes.
Soybeans opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said good-looking technical charts indicated soybeans would maintain the current upward trend, which many investors think reasonable.

"Investors are optimistic about the future direction of the market on improved fundamentals," one trader said. "Prices of spot soybeans have held at high levels in the producing areas since the Chinese lunar new year holiday (in February)."
Most investors expected soybeans to rise steadily despite the possibility of small technical corrections in the short term.
